name: Can you live in the house during a major home addition?

mainEntity.name: Can you live in the house during a major home addition in Los Angeles?
mainEntity.text: Can you live in the house during a major home addition in Los Angeles?

acceptedAnswer.text: Whether you can stay in the home during a major addition depends on the scope and how much of the house remains usable. If the work is isolated to one area and utilities stay mostly intact, living on-site may be realistic. If the project involves major structural work, roof removal, bathroom shutdowns, or repeated utility interruptions, temporary relocation may be the safer and less stressful option. Second-story additions and large tie-ins are usually the hardest to live through because they affect access, privacy, noise, and dust levels. Families with children, pets, or remote work needs often find the disruption greater than expected. Even if the house remains technically habitable, daily life can become difficult. Homeowners should ask the contractor for a phasing plan before starting. The plan should show which spaces will be unavailable, how dust and debris will be controlled, and whether water, power, or HVAC will be interrupted. That planning step helps determine whether staying in the house is practical or whether a temporary move makes more sense.
acceptedAnswer.description: Many homeowners can stay in the house during a home addition, but it depends on dust, noise, utility shutoffs, bathroom access, and whether the kitchen or sleeping areas are affected. Second-story and whole-house tie-in projects are usually harder to live through.
